vulnerabilities.description: Weak cryptographic randomness for session token generation. Fallback uses Math.random() instead of crypto.randomUUID(). While the code prefers crypto.randomUUID(), the fallback at line 21 is inadequate for security-sensitive tokens. Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and can be predicted.
Weak randomness in ID generation: Math.random().toString(16).slice(2) + Date.now().toString(16). This fallback pattern is predictable and unsuitable for security tokens or session identifiers.

Sensitive token stored in global window object. `window.__IMPECCABLE_TOKEN__` is accessible to any JavaScript in the page, including third-party scripts and XSS payloads. Token should be stored securely (HttpOnly cookie or encrypted memory storage).

Sensitive session data stored in localStorage without encryption. Session information including session ID and checkpoint revisions are stored as plaintext JSON. localStorage is vulnerable to XSS attacks and persistent to page navigation.

No validation of injected token and port values. The script blindly trusts `window.__IMPECCABLE_TOKEN__` and `window.__IMPECCABLE_PORT__` without validating their format, origin, or authenticity. Could allow injection of malicious values.

Potential XSS via inline style concatenation. While the code has some protection (CSS.escape usage elsewhere), dynamic style/class injection patterns could be exploited if user content reaches styling contexts without proper sanitization.

Unvalidated localStorage access. The code silently fails when localStorage is unavailable but doesn't distinguish between storage quota exceeded, private mode, or other security contexts. This could mask actual security issues.

No Content Security Policy (CSP) directives visible. Injected script lacks CSP headers to restrict what the injected code can do. An attacker could potentially exfiltrate data or perform unauthorized actions.

recommendations: Replace all Math.random() usage with crypto.getRandomValues() for generating security tokens and session IDs. Never use Math.random() for cryptographic purposes.
Move authentication tokens from window object and localStorage to HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies managed server-side. Sensitive tokens should never be accessible to client-side JavaScript.
Encrypt session data before storing in localStorage using a client-side encryption library (e.g., TweetNaCl.js). Include expiration checks.
Validate the format, origin, and authenticity of `window.__IMPECCABLE_TOKEN__` and `window.__IMPECCABLE_PORT__` before use. Implement CSRF tokens and origin verification.
Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers restricting script-src, limiting external connections, and preventing unsafe inline styles.
Add comprehensive input validation and output encoding for all user-controlled data before using in DOM manipulation, styles, or HTML contexts.
Use a security-focused markdown parser (e.g., DOMPurify) to sanitize user-generated markdown before rendering.
Implement subresource integrity (SRI) checks for all injected external scripts.
Add request signing (HMAC or similar) for sensitive API calls to prevent token replay attacks.
Audit all dependencies for known vulnerabilities. The bundled code shows signs of large build artifacts that may contain vulnerable libraries (review package-lock.json and bun.lock).
